g.text: Study 02 — band → event → ticket, and fourteen ways to never sell a seat twice
It spans rows. No single-row constraint on
ticket can express it, so every design must
decide WHERE the capacity check lives and
WHAT serialises two buyers reaching for the
a locked seat row · a locked parent row ·
a counter row · a unique index · the
isolation level · a pool of seat tokens ·
FOR UPDATE on the lowest free seat row
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + exact sold-out fallback
no lock; compare-and-set UPDATE, random start seat, retry
FOR UPDATE on the event row, then count
up to 8 counter rows per event, SKIP LOCKED
pre-created narrow slot rows; delete one, insert the ticket
